brief: UBS revises its Fed call after August jobs data. Non-farm payrolls rose 162,000, private payrolls 127,000 versus 55,000 consensus, plus 55,000 in upward revisions, lifting the three-month private-payroll average to 75,000, above the 0-60,000 breakeven range, while unemployment held at 4.1% as participation rose. This followed a July PCE inflation beat (3.7% y/y) and hawkish Jackson Hole comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh demanding inflation move to target clearly and at sufficient speed. Together these moved market-implied September hike odds from about 50% to 60%. UBS now expects two 25bp hikes in 2026 (September, December), taking fed funds to 4.00-4.25%, reversing its prior no-change-through-2026 call, though a second hike could be skipped if inflation cools enough through October. UBS raises 2-year and 10-year Treasury yield forecasts to 4.25% and 4.5% by June 2027, stays constructive on equities favoring AI, power and resources, and longevity, no longer favors locking in short-duration bond yields versus cash, sees near-term dollar support, and views gold as a portfolio hedge rather than a tactical Fed trade given near-term headwinds from higher real rates and a stronger dollar.
